newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Egis plummets on bourse after 9-mo results.
newsitem.headline: Egis plummets on bourse after 9-mo results.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar's shares plunged more than five percent on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday after the release of what analysts called slack January to September figures.
Egis shares opened at 8,900 forints, below Monday's close of 9,000 forints, and fell rapidly to end at 8,500, down 500.
Analysts were divided as to whether the figures were short of expectations.
"They (the results) are definitely lower than what we were expecting," said Frances Cloud at Nomura Equity Research in London. "And this seems to be for one reason alone -- weak domestic sales."
Egis's total sales rose to 17.35 billion forints from 14.44 billion over the same period of 1995.
Of this, the company generated 9.475 billion forints in the domestic market, 19.5 percent more than the 7.93 billion in the same nine months of 1995.
In September Hungary's year-on-year consumer price inflation stood at 22.2 percent.
Cloud noted that while Egis increased its domestic sales by 19.5 percent in the first nine months of 1996, the increase was 34.8 percent for peer company Richter.
In addition, Egis is more exposed to the domestic market which accounts for more than 50 percent of its sales as against around one-third for Richter.
In its results report Egis said that its turnover in July and August has been traditionally low because wholesalers make stockpiling usually in June, ahead of the summer off-season.
"In operating level the results met our expectations," said Barna Papay, ING Barings' Budapest-based analyst. "The third quarter is always weaker for seasonal reasons."
Egis reported operating profits advancing to 3.55 billion forints in the January-September period from 3.07 billion in the same nine months of 1995.

ING Barings' London-based analyst told Reuters in October that the pharmaceuticals' third quarter was generally weaker than other quarters because price increases occur in the first quarter and wholesalers pile stocks ahead of the rises.
Nevertheless, Egis was mostly in line with its annual profit plan and analysts believed it would meet its target.
Its nine-month pre-tax profits of 4.08 billion forints, which rose from 3.83 billion forints, represent 72 percent of the annual plan, Egis said in the report.

"One can expect costs and expenditures to be in line with plans in the fourth quarter," Egis said. "Therefore the annual pre-tax profit -- pending mainly on the turnover -- could be expected between 5.5 and 6.0 billion forints." Egis predicted its annual sales revenues between 24 billion and 25 billion.
Looking forward to a strong fourth quarter Papay forecast the company would meet its plans.
"We expect Egis to have a strong fourth quarter because wholesalers will stockpile ahead of the price rises," he said.
